purpose: Create the fourth scaled-agent lane-depth and public-explainability packet set for Agriculture, International affairs, and Transportation/infrastructure.

lane_packets.what_it_does: Tracks federal farm income stabilization, crop insurance, agricultural research, inspection, market support, and general agricultural services while keeping food and nutrition assistance in the income-security lane.

what_taxpayers_pay_now.required_next: official multi-year agriculture path, support-versus-insurance-versus-services bridge, market-price-support treatment, farm and acre denominators, and outcome floors

lane_packets.who_is_served_or_protected: Farmers, ranchers, agricultural producers, crop-insurance participants, rural communities, consumers affected by food and market stability, and taxpayers funding agricultural support and services.
lane_packets.overspending_underfunding_boundary: Subsidy levels, insurance losses, indemnities, or improper-payment estimates are review-needed signals only. They are not savings estimates, waste findings, fraud findings, market-price-support targets, or instructions to cut farm programs.
lane_packets.technology_transition_boundary: Crop-insurance data systems, acreage reporting, remote sensing, claims validation, producer services, market data, privacy, appeals, false-positive controls, and delivery continuity must be costed before any modernization credit.
lane_packets.scope_boundary: Food and nutrition assistance is function 600 income security, not function 350 agriculture.
lane_packets.component_separation_boundary: Budget support, insurance, general services, and market-price support must be distinguished before any policy scenario or benchmark use.
lane_packets.payment_integrity_boundary: Federal crop-insurance integrity work can identify measurement gaps and review tasks, but improper-payment facts do not prove fraud and do not create recoverable savings without causal prevention or same-cohort collection lineage.
blocked_evidence: budget support versus insurance versus services bridge
farm, acre, production, and risk denominators

lane_packets.what_it_does: Tracks diplomacy, development, humanitarian aid, security assistance, foreign information and exchange, and international financial programs while keeping each instrument separate.

what_taxpayers_pay_now.required_next: official multi-year component paths, commitments-versus-outlays bridge, recipient and instrument decomposition, financial-program risk treatment, and outcome floors

lane_packets.who_is_served_or_protected: US national-interest missions, diplomatic posts, aid recipients, humanitarian beneficiaries, security partners, exchange participants, and taxpayers exposed to grant, loan, deposit, and foreign-policy risks.
lane_packets.overspending_underfunding_boundary: Peer spending differences, negative net financing, aid levels, or security-assistance volumes are review-needed signals only. International spending differences are not savings, and negative financial-program outlays are not fraud recovery or automatic savings.
lane_packets.technology_transition_boundary: Grant management, procurement, aid delivery, monitoring, sanctions/controls, financial-instrument accounting, cyber risk, field access, and mission continuity must be costed before any modernization credit.
lane_packets.component_separation_boundary: Diplomacy, ODA, humanitarian, security assistance, information/exchange, and financial instruments must stay separate; no composite target is published.
lane_packets.negative_financial_program_boundary: The negative international-financial-program line is an accounting result driven mainly by FMS customer deposits exceeding same-year trust-fund outlays; it is not negative diplomacy, aid, fraud recovery, or automatic savings.
blocked_evidence: matched diplomatic and ODA peer scope

lane_packets.what_it_does: Tracks federal ground, air, water, and other transportation commitments, including the transportation pilot's baseline, floor, modernization, stress, source-custody, and trust-fund accounting scaffolds.

what_taxpayers_pay_now.required_next: FY2032-FY2035 official annual rows, trust-fund annual values, gross-to-net reconciliation, federal-state-local translation, asset inventory, maintenance gap, safety floors, and floor thresholds

lane_packets.who_is_served_or_protected: Travelers, freight users, state and local infrastructure partners, airport and airway users, highway users, water transportation users, communities affected by access and safety, and taxpayers funding transportation commitments.
lane_packets.overspending_underfunding_boundary: High costs, project delays, trust-fund gaps, backlog, or peer differences are review-needed signals only until federal/state/local scope, trust-fund flows, asset condition, maintenance gap, safety, and delivery floors are matched.
lane_packets.technology_transition_boundary: Asset-management systems, project delivery analytics, permitting, procurement, fraud/error controls, safety data, cyber risk, state/local implementation capacity, and transition/admin/monitoring costs must be costed before any modernization credit.
lane_packets.trust_fund_boundary: Highway Trust Fund and Airport and Airway Trust Fund values must remain separate, general-fund transfers must be explicit, and annual trust-fund values are still missing.
blocked_evidence: annual Highway Trust Fund receipts, outgo, and balance
annual Airport and Airway Trust Fund receipts, outgo, and balance

plain_english_status: Wave 4 now has component-heavy and pilot lane-depth explainability scaffolds for Agriculture, International affairs, and Transportation/infrastructure. Transportation remains the deepest pilot lane, but it is still incomplete because FY2032-FY2035 federal rows, annual trust-fund values, federal/state/local translation, floor thresholds, and floor pass reports are missing. This packet does not complete lane depth, calculate rates, publish target costs, claim savings, identify waste or fraud, direct department cuts, claim technology savings, run the solver, or claim a balanced budget.
